reviews.body: Yes please. This would have saved ops an afternoon.
Approving, one question inline for the record.

comments.author: carol
comments.body: For the record, what about inbound webhooks? We'll have the Stripe receiver at some point and those are POSTs that move money too (payout.paid, charge.refunded). Stripe won't send our `Idempotency-Key` header, so this decorator would 400 every event.

comments.author: alice
comments.body: Right, webhooks are a different case. This rule is about our own clients retrying our API. Provider webhooks don't carry our key, but every Stripe event has a unique event id, so the receiver dedupes on that instead. We'll write that down when we build the receiver. For every endpoint our clients call, the rule is simple: moves money, gets `@idempotent`.

comments.author: dan
comments.body: Will the 400 break older app versions that don't send the header yet? Or is the mobile release going out before this merges?

comments.author: alice
comments.body:
Only refunds is decorated in this PR. The mobile app has sent the header on refunds since
4.12, and older versions are under 2% of refund traffic; a 400 for them beats another
duplicate refund. Charges and captures wait for the 02-09 release.
